title: The Explicit Cramer Solution: xᵢ = det(Aᵢ)/det A
description: Answers the parent's OQ-01: formalize the classical scalar form of Cramer's rule, xᵢ = det(Aᵢ)/det A, where Aᵢ is A with its i-th column replaced by b, as an equality over a field with det A ≠ 0. The parent (cramers-rule-oq-04-oq-01) proved only the determinant form A·(adj A · b) = (det A)·b. Here we close the gap to the honest scalar formula by bridging through Mathlib's Matrix.cramer: cramer_apply identifies its i-th component with det(Aᵢ), and the same adjugate identity adj(A)·A = (det A)·I that powers the parent shows the cramer vector equals (det A)·x for any solution x of Ax = b. We also prove existence (the formula solves the system) and uniqueness of the solution. 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext:
Cramer's rule (Gabriel Cramer, 1750) gives a closed-form solution to a square linear system Ax = b when det A ≠ 0: the i-th unknown equals det(Aᵢ)/det A, where Aᵢ is the matrix obtained from A by replacing its i-th column with the right-hand side b. It is the determinant-theoretic counterpart of A⁻¹ = (det A)⁻¹·adj A, since (adj A · b)ᵢ = det(Aᵢ) by cofactor expansion along column i. While impractical for computation, the rule is theoretically central: it makes the solution an explicit rational function of the entries, which is what powers its use in proofs (continuity/algebraicity of solutions, Cramer–Gauss bounds, the Laplace expansion).

The parent entry formalized only the determinant-scaled form A·(adj A · b) = (det A)·b. The honest scalar statement requires dividing by det A and identifying each adjugate-vector component with the column-replaced determinant. Mathlib supplies exactly this bridge in Matrix.cramer: by definition cramer A b i = det(A.updateCol i b) (cramer_apply), and cramer A b = adjugate A *ᵥ b (cramer_eq_adjugate_mulVec). This entry assembles the classical formula and its existence/uniqueness companions from those primitives.
overview.problemStatement: Over a field K, given A : Matrix n n K, vectors x, b with A *ᵥ x = b, and det A ≠ 0, prove the explicit Cramer formula x i = det(A.updateCol i b) / det A. Establish the algebraic core over an arbitrary commutative ring (no invertibility), and prove that the closed-form vector both solves the system and is its unique solution.
overview.proofStrategy: The algebraic core det_smul_solution_eq_cramer proves (det A)·x = cramer A b without any invertibility: rewrite cramer A b = adjugate A *ᵥ b (cramer_eq_adjugate_mulVec), substitute b = A *ᵥ x, and collapse adjugate A *ᵥ (A *ᵥ x) = (adjugate A * A) *ᵥ x = ((det A)•1) *ᵥ x = (det A)·x via mulVec_mulVec, adjugate_mul, smul_mulVec, one_mulVec. Taking the i-th component and rewriting with cramer_apply gives (det A)·xᵢ = det(Aᵢ) (det_mul_solution_eq_det_updateCol). Over a field with det A ≠ 0, eq_div_iff turns the goal xᵢ = det(Aᵢ)/det A into (det A)·xᵢ = det(Aᵢ), which is exactly the core (cramer_solution). Uniqueness follows because both solutions equal the same closed-form vector. Existence (cramer_formula_isSolution) writes the formula as A.det⁻¹ • cramer A b and uses mulVec_cramer (A *ᵥ cramer A b = (det A)·b) plus inv_mul_cancel₀ to recover b.
keyInsights: The scalar Cramer formula factors through one ring-level identity: (det A)·x = cramer A b holds over ANY commutative ring whenever Ax = b — no invertibility, no field. Division enters only at the very last step.

cramer_apply is the dictionary between the abstract adjugate vector and the concrete column-replaced determinant: cramer A b i = det(A.updateCol i b). Without it the 'det(Aᵢ)' in the statement would be disconnected from the adjugate machinery.

The same adjugate identity adj(A)·A = (det A)·I that the parent used to prove the determinant form A·(adj A · b) = (det A)·b is what collapses the cramer vector here — the two entries are two readings of one identity.

Existence and uniqueness are cleanly separated: uniqueness needs only that every solution equals the closed form; existence needs mulVec_cramer and a single scalar cancellation. Together they show the system has exactly one solution, given explicitly.
Over a field, det A ≠ 0 ⟺ A invertible, so the hypothesis is the sharp one; the formula then computes A⁻¹b coordinate-by-coordinate as a ratio of determinants.

sections.summary: States the parent's open question OQ-01 — promote the determinant-scaled solution A·(adj A · b) = (det A)·b to the honest scalar formula xᵢ = det(Aᵢ)/det A — and names the bridge: Matrix.cramer, whose i-th component cramer_apply identifies with det(Aᵢ), collapses to (det A)·x via the same adjugate identity the parent used. Lists the five main results (det_smul_solution_eq_cramer, cramer_solution, cramer_solution_eq, cramer_solution_unique, cramer_formula_isSolution) before opening the Matrix namespace and fixing the ambient commutative-ring section.
sections.mathContext: Bridges the parent's determinant form $A\cdot(\mathrm{adj}\,A\cdot b) = (\det A)\cdot b$ to the scalar formula $x_i = \det(A_i)/\det A$ via $\mathrm{cramer}\,A\,b\,i = \det(A.\mathrm{updateCol}\,i\,b)$.

sections.title: Section I: The Invertibility-Free Algebraic Core
sections.summary: det_smul_solution_eq_cramer ((det A)·x = cramer A b for any commutative ring) and its scalar form det_mul_solution_eq_det_updateCol ((det A)·xᵢ = det(Aᵢ)), via cramer_eq_adjugate_mulVec + adjugate_mul + cramer_apply.
sections.mathContext: The entire content of Cramer's rule before any division: scaling a solution by the determinant reproduces the column-replaced determinants.

sections.title: Section II: The Explicit Formula
sections.summary: cramer_solution: xᵢ = det(Aᵢ)/det A over a field with det A ≠ 0 — the OQ's literal target, obtained from the algebraic core by eq_div_iff. cramer_solution_eq packages this componentwise result as the full closed-form vector x = fun i => det(Aᵢ)/det A.
sections.mathContext: Division by the nonzero determinant turns the invertibility-free algebraic core into the classical scalar formula stated in every textbook.

sections.title: Section III: Uniqueness
sections.summary: cramer_solution_unique: any two solutions x, y of A x = b coincide when det A ≠ 0, since both must equal the same closed form cramer_solution_eq produces. Uniqueness alone needs no cancellation — it is immediate once every solution is pinned to one formula.
sections.mathContext: Together with cramer_formula_isSolution (existence, below) this shows Ax = b has exactly one solution when det A ≠ 0, given explicitly in closed form.

sections.title: Section IV: Existence — the Formula Solves the System
sections.summary: cramer_formula_isSolution: A *ᵥ (fun i => det(Aᵢ)/det A) = b, writing the formula as A.det⁻¹ • cramer A b and cancelling via mulVec_cramer and inv_mul_cancel₀.
sections.mathContext: Combined with uniqueness, the system Ax = b has exactly one solution, given in closed form.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 109 lines and 6 theorems formalizing the classical scalar form of Cramer's rule. The headline cramer_solution proves xᵢ = det(Aᵢ)/det A over a field with det A ≠ 0; det_smul_solution_eq_cramer isolates the invertibility-free core (det A)·x = cramer A b over any commutative ring; cramer_solution_unique and cramer_formula_isSolution give uniqueness and existence of the solution.
conclusion.implications: This closes the parent's OQ-01: where the parent proved only the determinant form A·(adj A · b) = (det A)·b, this entry delivers the honest scalar formula every textbook states, with the column-replaced determinant det(A.updateCol i b) supplied by Mathlib's cramer_apply. The clean separation — an invertibility-free core over a commutative ring, with division deferred to the final field step — is reusable wherever Cramer's rule appears (e.g. algebraicity/continuity of linear-system solutions).
